title: Simple Non-Verbal Sentences
lede: Build clear present-time statements of identity, description and location without inserting an English-style “to be” verb.

items.prompt: Which Arabic sentence means “He is an engineer”?
items.feedback: In a present-time equational sentence, Arabic normally uses no separate “is”.

items.prompt: Which is a complete sentence meaning “The house is large”?
items.feedback: A definite subject followed by an indefinite predicate forms a complete statement.

items.prompt: Choose the correct feminine form.
items.feedback: The predicate noun matches the female person in gender.

items.prompt: Which means “I am in the bank”?
items.feedback: The prepositional phrase functions as the predicate.

items.prompt: Which demonstrative matches سَيَّارَةٌ?
items.feedback: سَيَّارَةٌ is feminine singular.

items.prompt: Which is an adjective phrase rather than a complete sentence?
items.feedback: Both words are definite, so they form “the large classroom”, not “The classroom is large”.

items.prompt: Choose “The teacher (f.) is active.”
items.feedback: The predicate agrees in gender and remains indefinite.

items.prompt: Choose “The two boys are ready.”
items.feedback: A dual human subject takes a dual predicate.

items.prompt: Choose “The books are useful.”
items.feedback: A non-human plural normally takes feminine singular agreement.

items.prompt: Choose the location sentence.
items.feedback: The prepositional phrase is the predicate.

items.prompt: Which statement contains no present-tense copula?
items.feedback: Present equational Arabic normally joins subject and predicate directly.

items.prompt: Identify the predicate in الْجَوُّ جَمِيلٌ.
items.feedback: جَمِيلٌ tells us something about the subject.

items.prompt: Choose “This is a new car.”
items.feedback: The demonstrative and adjective match the feminine singular noun.

items.prompt: Choose the complete sentence.
items.feedback: Definite subject + indefinite predicate.

items.prompt: Choose “We are at home.”
items.feedback: The noun after فِي is genitive.

items.prompt: Which human plural agreement is correct?
items.feedback: Human masculine plural uses plural agreement.

items.prompt: Which non-human plural agreement is correct?
items.feedback: Non-human plurals normally take feminine singular agreement.

items.prompt: Which phrase is not yet a full statement?
items.feedback: Matching definiteness makes an adjective phrase.

items.prompt: Choose “The children are in the garden.”
items.feedback: A prepositional phrase can be the predicate.

items.prompt: Best editing question?
options: Is the subject clear, and does a single-word predicate agree with it?
Does every predicate begin with ال?
items.feedback: Present nominal sentences need clarity and agreement, not an inserted copula.

games.e: Both words are definite: “the large house”.
Definite subject + indefinite predicate: “The house is large.”
The prepositional phrase is the predicate.
The definite adjective stays inside the noun phrase.
The indefinite adjective is the predicate.
The feminine singular adjective is definite and attributive.
Non-human plural subject + feminine singular predicate.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا تَهُمُّ الْجُمْلَةُ الِاسْمِيَّةُ؟
Arabic can state identity, description and location without a present-tense form of “to be”.
### Core
Build a clear subject + predicate sentence without adding an unnecessary verb.
### Develop
Control gender, number, definiteness and prepositional predicates.
### Stretch
Recognise case-aware models and distinguish several predicate types.
[callout] Communication target: identify people and things, describe them and say where they are in natural Modern Standard Arabic.
## Diagnostic start
Use this as a low-stakes readiness check, not as a final test.
## The present equational sentence
Arabic normally places the subject and predicate beside one another; English supplies am/is/are in translation.
[callout] Core pattern: الْمُبْتَدَأُ + الْخَبَرُ — subject/topic + information about it.

TABLE: Function | Arabic model | Meaning // Identity | هُوَ مُهَنْدِسٌ. | He is an engineer. // Description | الْجَوُّ جَمِيلٌ. | The weather is beautiful. // Classification | هَذَا كِتَابٌ. | This is a book. // Location | أَنَا فِي الْبَنْكِ. | I am in the bank.
[callout/warning] Common transfer error: Do not insert يَكُونُ simply because English contains “is”. هُوَ مُهَنْدِسٌ is the natural present statement.
## Agreement in single-word predicates
A noun or adjective predicate should fit the intended person or noun in gender and number.

TABLE: Subject type | Model | Decision // masculine singular | هُوَ طَالِبٌ مُجْتَهِدٌ. | masculine singular // feminine singular | هِيَ طَالِبَةٌ مُجْتَهِدَةٌ. | feminine singular // masculine dual | الطَّالِبَانِ مُسْتَعِدَّانِ. | dual // human masculine plural | الطُّلَّابُ مُجْتَهِدُونَ. | human plural // human feminine plural | الطَّالِبَاتُ مُجْتَهِدَاتٌ. | human feminine plural // non-human plural | الْكُتُبُ مُفِيدَةٌ. | feminine singular
[callout] Boundary: full case endings help explain the structure, but communicative control comes first. The later Case Endings package will analyse them systematically.
## Phrase or complete sentence?
Definiteness often reveals whether the adjective belongs inside a noun phrase or acts as the predicate.

TABLE: Form | Meaning | Analysis // الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرُ | the large house | definite noun phrase // الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ. | The house is large. | complete nominal sentence // مَدْرَسَةٌ جَدِيدَةٌ | a new school | indefinite noun phrase // الْمَدْرَسَةُ جَدِيدَةٌ. | The school is new. | complete nominal sentence
[callout/warning] Do not confuse: الطَّالِبُ الْمُجْتَهِدُ names “the hardworking student”; الطَّالِبُ مُجْتَهِدٌ states “The student is hardworking.”
## Three practical predicate types
A predicate may be one word, a prepositional phrase or a locator/adverbial expression.

TABLE: Predicate type | Model | What it tells us // single noun/adjective | أَخِي طَبِيبٌ. | identity or description // prepositional phrase | أَخِي فِي الْمُسْتَشْفَى. | location // locator phrase | الْمَدْرَسَةُ أَمَامَ الْمَسْجِدِ. | relative position // time expression | الِامْتِحَانُ غَدًا. | when
[callout] Useful feature: a prepositional predicate does not change for masculine/feminine agreement: هُوَ فِي الْبَيْتِ and هِيَ فِي الْبَيْتِ .
## Misconception clinic
Repair the structure, then explain the decision.

TABLE: Draft | Improved version | Reason // هُوَ يَكُونُ مُعَلِّمًا. | هُوَ مُعَلِّمٌ. | No present copula is needed. // هِيَ طَبِيبٌ. | هِيَ طَبِيبَةٌ. | Gender agreement. // الْبَيْتُ الْكَبِيرُ. | الْبَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ. | The intended meaning is a complete statement. // أَنَا فِي الْبَنْكُ. | أَنَا فِي الْبَنْكِ. | The noun after فِي is genitive. // السَّيَّارَاتُ سَرِيعَاتٌ. | السَّيَّارَاتُ سَرِيعَةٌ. | Non-human plural → feminine singular agreement.
## Game: Phrase or sentence?
Read for meaning and definiteness, not just word order.
## Skills workshop
Use nominal sentences to describe a person, place and everyday situation.
[ar] هَذِهِ مَدْرَسَتِي. هِيَ كَبِيرَةٌ وَحَدِيثَةٌ، وَالْمَكْتَبَةُ فِي الطَّابِقِ الْأَوَّلِ.
[ar] أَنَا طَالِبَةٌ. مَادَّتِي الْمُفَضَّلَةُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ، وَصَفِّي قُرْبَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
### Describe a person and a place
Write 80–100 Arabic words introducing yourself or another person and describing a familiar place.
[callout] Success checklist: Use at least four single-word predicates, three prepositional/locator predicates, correct gender agreement and one non-human plural.
[callout] Paper route: Write the paragraph, underline each subject once and box each predicate. Label one predicate “word” and one “phrase”.
## Final mastery check
Apply the complete present-time nominal-sentence system.
### What you can now do
- Build present equational sentences without an unnecessary copula.
- Distinguish noun phrases from complete statements.
- Use noun, adjective, prepositional and locator predicates.
- Apply human and non-human agreement accurately.
Spaced revisit: describe the same room again in three days without looking at the models.
